1	---
2	title: 'Narrative-Independent Raw-Data Download'
3	type: 'feature'
4	created: '2026-11-07'
5	status: 'done'
6	review_loop_iteration: 0
7	context: []
8	baseline_commit: '753d448f4e84e41655e9291a5efd56999154bf6b'
9	---
10	
11	<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
12	
13	## Intent
14	
15	**Problem:** Spec-7-1 left both download buttons `onPressed: null` and folded `data_ready` into the same visual as `processing` — raw data is never actually downloadable, even once the backend has it ready ahead of the narrative.
16	
17	**Approach:** Wire `GET /export/:jobId/download` behind both buttons (open the signed URL externally, never buffer it in-app), and give `data_ready` its own state so the sheet shows "Baixar dados brutos" already enabled while the narrative keeps processing underneath.
18	
19	## Boundaries & Constraints
20	
21	**Always:**
22	- Call `export-download-get` by function name, `jobId` trailing, `format=pdf|raw` query param.
23	- Capture the `302`'s `Location` header directly (`followRedirects: false` + a permissive `validateStatus`) — never auto-follow into the signed-storage host.
24	- Open the signed URL externally (new `DownloadOpener` port, `url_launcher`-backed) — never buffer/write the file in-app.
25	- `data_ready` → its own `ExportJobState.dataReady()`: same progress-bar/text as `generating`, plus the now-enabled raw button beneath.
26	- A download failure shows an inline `SnackBar` (mirrors `_onExportTap`'s create-failure pattern), never mutates the sheet's job-status content.
27	
28	**Ask First:** None — docs/input is silent on how a finished file reaches the user; external-open vs. in-app buffering is decided here.
29	
30	**Never:** add a new `Failure` subtype for download errors (reuse `Failure.fromCode`, AD-3); touch empty-period state/copy (Story 7.3); add a busy state to `AppButton` itself (deferred).
31	
32	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
33	
34	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output | Error Handling |
35	|----------|--------------|------------------|-----------------|
36	| Hybrid state | `status=data_ready`, `narrativeStatus=processing` | Progress bar + text + enabled "Baixar dados brutos" | N/A |
37	| Raw/PDF tap | Tap enabled button | `GET export-download-get?format=raw\|pdf` → opens URL externally | Failure → `SnackBar`, state unchanged |
38	| Narrative failed/skipped | `status=done`, `narrativeStatus in {failed,skipped}` | Only raw button, now enabled | N/A |
39	| Missing `Location` | `302` with no header | `Failure.malformedResponse` | Same `SnackBar` path |
40	
41	</frozen-after-approval>
42	
43	## Code Map
44	
45	- `lib/core/network/api_client.dart:79` -- new `getRedirectLocation(function, {pathParams, queryParameters})`: `_dio.get<dynamic>`, `followRedirects: false` + permissive `validateStatus`, reads `response.headers.value('location')`; don't override `responseType` — error bodies stay JSON so `_mapDioException`/`dioErrorCodeOf` keep working unchanged
46	- `lib/features/export/domain/entities/export_job_state.dart:28` -- add `ExportJobState.dataReady()` + `ExportJobDataReady` (mirror `ExportJobPreparing`'s no-field shape)
47	- `lib/features/export/domain/entities/export_download_format.dart` (new) -- `enum ExportDownloadFormat { pdf, raw }`
48	- `lib/features/export/domain/services/download_opener.dart` (new) -- abstract `DownloadOpener { Future<bool> open(String url); }`, mirrors `chat/domain/services/connectivity_watcher.dart`'s port shape
49	- `lib/features/export/data/services/url_launcher_download_opener.dart` (new) -- `launchUrl(Uri.parse(url), mode: LaunchMode.externalApplication)`
50	- `export_repository.dart:30` / `export_remote_data_source.dart:77` / `export_repository_impl.dart:31` -- add `getDownloadUrl(jobId, {required format})` through all three layers; data source calls `_apiClient.getRedirectLocation('export-download-get', pathParams: [jobId], queryParameters: {'format': format.name})`
51	- `lib/features/export/data/models/export_job_status_dto.dart:55-60` -- split `'data_ready'` out of `'processing'`
52	- `lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart` -- inject `DownloadOpener`; add `Failure? lastDownloadFailure`, `downloadPdf()`/`downloadRawData()` (delegate to private `_download(ExportDownloadFormat)` using stored `_jobId`); `_isTerminal` unchanged
53	- `lib/features/export/presentation/widgets/export_status_sheet.dart:134-220` -- `_contentFor`/`_doneContent` gain `context`+`cubit`; new `ExportJobDataReady()` case; both buttons wired via new `_handleDownload` (shows `SnackBar` with `cubit.lastDownloadFailure?.message` on failure)
54	- `lib/features/export/export_injection.dart:17-27` -- register `DownloadOpener`, inject into `ExportJobCubit`'s factory
55	- `test/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit_test.dart` -- `_FakeExportRepository` needs `getDownloadUrl`; add `_FakeDownloadOpener`
56	- `pubspec.yaml` -- add `url_launcher` (`fvm flutter pub add url_launcher`)
57	- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1550-1580`, `export-screen-states.md` -- contract + hybrid-row authority
58	
59	## Tasks & Acceptance
60	
61	**Execution:** one task per Code Map bullet above, in that order, plus:
62	- [x] Unit tests: `getRedirectLocation` (success/missing-location/error-status), `getDownloadUrl`, `toState()`'s `data_ready`, cubit download methods
63	- [x] Widget tests: hybrid-state render, both `done` buttons call through, download failure → `SnackBar` with state unchanged
64	
65	**Acceptance Criteria:**
66	- Given `status=data_ready`/`narrativeStatus=processing`, when polled, then "Baixar dados brutos" is already enabled and downloads via `GET /export/:jobId/download` while summary-progress text stays visible underneath.
67	- Given the narrative fails/is skipped at `status=done`, then "Baixar dados brutos" stays enabled, error copy stays scoped to the narrative.
68	- Given the narrative succeeds at `status=done`, then both "Baixar PDF" and "Baixar dados brutos" are enabled and tappable.
69	
70	## Spec Change Log
71	
72	## Design Notes
73	
74	- Download mechanism (docs/input silent): open the signed URL externally via `url_launcher` rather than buffering bytes in-app — no storage permissions, no local file/share-sheet plumbing.
75	- Download-tap failures surface via `SnackBar`, not a cubit state transition — the sealed `ExportJobState` models job *progress*, not one-off actions; a transient failure must never mutate the displayed state.
76	
77	## Verification
78	
79	**Commands:**
80	- `fvm flutter pub add url_launcher` -- resolves cleanly
81	- `fvm flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` -- no conflicts
82	- `fvm flutter analyze` -- zero issues
83	- `fvm flutter test` -- all pass
84	
85	## Suggested Review Order
86	
87	**Redirect-based download (entry point)**
88	
89	- The one place a non-JSON, `302`-shaped response is handled: `followRedirects: false` + a permissive `validateStatus`, error bodies still decode as JSON so existing error-mapping is untouched.
90	  [`api_client.dart:102`](../../lib/core/network/api_client.dart#L102)
91	
92	**Download wiring through the layers**
93	
94	- The port every other layer calls through — `jobId` + `format` in, signed URL out.
95	  [`export_repository.dart:41`](../../lib/features/export/domain/repositories/export_repository.dart#L41)
96	
97	- Resolves to `export-download-get` by function name, `format.name` as the query value verbatim.
98	  [`export_remote_data_source.dart:85`](../../lib/features/export/data/datasources/export_remote_data_source.dart#L85)
99	
100	- Thin pass-through, no cache — same shape as every other method on this repository.
101	  [`export_repository_impl.dart:34`](../../lib/features/export/data/repositories/export_repository_impl.dart#L34)
102	
103	**The hybrid `data_ready` state**
104	
105	- `data_ready` gets its own sealed case instead of folding into `generating` — the whole point of this story.
106	  [`export_job_state.dart:35`](../../lib/features/export/domain/entities/export_job_state.dart#L35)
107	
108	- Where the DTO's raw `status` string is split into this new case.
109	  [`export_job_status_dto.dart:59`](../../lib/features/export/data/models/export_job_status_dto.dart#L59)
110	
111	**Cubit download lifecycle (review-patch round)**
112	
113	- `_download`'s own shape after review: in-flight guard, `jobId == null` and a throwing opener both map to `Failure`, returned directly rather than through a shared field.
114	  [`export_job_cubit.dart:161`](../../lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart#L161)
115	
116	- The guard itself — a second call while one is in flight is a no-op, mirroring `_pollInFlight`.
117	  [`export_job_cubit.dart:145`](../../lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart#L145)
118	
119	- `downloadPdf`/`downloadRawData`'s own `Future<Failure?>` signature — what callers actually see.
120	  [`export_job_cubit.dart:148`](../../lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart#L148)
121	
122	**External-open port**
123	
124	- The domain port — never promises it won't throw, which is exactly why the cubit now guards its own call to it.
125	  [`download_opener.dart:11`](../../lib/features/export/domain/services/download_opener.dart#L11)
126	
127	- The real, `url_launcher`-backed implementation — catches internally so a malformed URL/platform failure degrades to `false`.

131	
132	- Reads the download method's own return value directly now — no more side-channel field the widget used to mutate.

- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1550-1580`, `export-screen-states.md` -- contract + hybrid-row authority

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:** one task per Code Map bullet above, in that order, plus:
- [x] Unit tests: `getRedirectLocation` (success/missing-location/error-status), `getDownloadUrl`, `toState()`'s `data_ready`, cubit download methods
- [x] Widget tests: hybrid-state render, both `done` buttons call through, download failure → `SnackBar` with state unchanged

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given `status=data_ready`/`narrativeStatus=processing`, when polled, then "Baixar dados brutos" is already enabled and downloads via `GET /export/:jobId/download` while summary-progress text stays visible underneath.
- Given the narrative fails/is skipped at `status=done`, then "Baixar dados brutos" stays enabled, error copy stays scoped to the narrative.
- Given the narrative succeeds at `status=done`, then both "Baixar PDF" and "Baixar dados brutos" are enabled and tappable.

## Spec Change Log

## Design Notes

- Download mechanism (docs/input silent): open the signed URL externally via `url_launcher` rather than buffering bytes in-app — no storage permissions, no local file/share-sheet plumbing.
- Download-tap failures surface via `SnackBar`, not a cubit state transition — the sealed `ExportJobState` models job *progress*, not one-off actions; a transient failure must never mutate the displayed state.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter pub add url_launcher` -- resolves cleanly
- `fvm flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` -- no conflicts
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- zero issues
- `fvm flutter test` -- all pass

## Suggested Review Order

**Redirect-based download (entry point)**

- The one place a non-JSON, `302`-shaped response is handled: `followRedirects: false` + a permissive `validateStatus`, error bodies still decode as JSON so existing error-mapping is untouched.
  [`api_client.dart:102`](../../lib/core/network/api_client.dart#L102)

**Download wiring through the layers**

- The port every other layer calls through — `jobId` + `format` in, signed URL out.
  [`export_repository.dart:41`](../../lib/features/export/domain/repositories/export_repository.dart#L41)

- Resolves to `export-download-get` by function name, `format.name` as the query value verbatim.
  [`export_remote_data_source.dart:85`](../../lib/features/export/data/datasources/export_remote_data_source.dart#L85)

- Thin pass-through, no cache — same shape as every other method on this repository.
  [`export_repository_impl.dart:34`](../../lib/features/export/data/repositories/export_repository_impl.dart#L34)

**The hybrid `data_ready` state**

- `data_ready` gets its own sealed case instead of folding into `generating` — the whole point of this story.
  [`export_job_state.dart:35`](../../lib/features/export/domain/entities/export_job_state.dart#L35)

- Where the DTO's raw `status` string is split into this new case.
  [`export_job_status_dto.dart:59`](../../lib/features/export/data/models/export_job_status_dto.dart#L59)

**Cubit download lifecycle (review-patch round)**

- `_download`'s own shape after review: in-flight guard, `jobId == null` and a throwing opener both map to `Failure`, returned directly rather than through a shared field.
  [`export_job_cubit.dart:161`](../../lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart#L161)

- The guard itself — a second call while one is in flight is a no-op, mirroring `_pollInFlight`.
  [`export_job_cubit.dart:145`](../../lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart#L145)

- `downloadPdf`/`downloadRawData`'s own `Future<Failure?>` signature — what callers actually see.
  [`export_job_cubit.dart:148`](../../lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart#L148)

**External-open port**

- The domain port — never promises it won't throw, which is exactly why the cubit now guards its own call to it.
  [`download_opener.dart:11`](../../lib/features/export/domain/services/download_opener.dart#L11)

- The real, `url_launcher`-backed implementation — catches internally so a malformed URL/platform failure degrades to `false`.
  [`url_launcher_download_opener.dart:10`](../../lib/features/export/data/services/url_launcher_download_opener.dart#L10)

- Reads the download method's own return value directly now — no more side-channel field the widget used to mutate.
  [`export_status_sheet.dart:267`](../../lib/features/export/presentation/widgets/export_status_sheet.dart#L267)

  [`export_status_sheet.dart:162`](../../lib/features/export/presentation/widgets/export_status_sheet.dart#L162)

  [`export_status_sheet.dart:219`](../../lib/features/export/presentation/widgets/export_status_sheet.dart#L219)

- `DownloadOpener` registered alongside the rest of the feature, injected into the cubit's factory.

# Step 2: Review

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`
- All review subagents must run at the same model capability as the current session.
- Run subagents synchronously: launch them together, then wait for all results before continuing.

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. The review layers are `{workflow.review_layers}`, resolved during activation.

2. For each layer in `{workflow.review_layers}`:
   - `instruction` empty or missing → drop the layer silently (an override disabled it).
   - `when` condition present and not satisfied by the current context (`{review_mode}`, `{spec_file}`) → drop the layer and tell the user, e.g. "Acceptance Auditor skipped — no spec file provided."
   - otherwise → the layer is active.

   If no layer is active, HALT with status `blocked` and blocking condition `no active review layers`.

3. Execute all active layers in parallel wherever their execution methods allow: expand `{skill-root}` in each layer's `instruction` to this skill's absolute installed directory, then substitute the runtime placeholders (`{diff_output}`, `{spec_file}`). For an instruction that launches a reviewer subagent, launch that child with the prompt text after placeholder substitution; do not load the reviewer instruction file yourself. For any other customized instruction, execute it as written. Do not leave `{skill-root}` unresolved in a child prompt. If a layer's instruction requires subagents and subagents are not available, for each such layer write under `{implementation_artifacts}` the exact child prompt from that layer's instruction after placeholder substitution (not a path-only pointer), then HALT. Ask the user to run each in a separate session (ideally a different LLM) and paste back the findings. When findings are pasted, treat them as those layers' findings and resume from this point. This is the only allowed parent-side read of a reviewer instruction file.

4. **Layer failure handling**: If any layer fails, times out, or returns empty results, append the layer's `name` to `{failed_layers}` (comma-separated) and proceed with findings from the remaining layers.

  ### `followRedirects: false` on `getRedirectLocation` is never actually exercised by either test that claims to cover it
  
  - **Changed surface:** `lib/core/network/api_client.dart:102-124` — the new `ApiClient.getRedirectLocation` builds `Options(followRedirects: false, validateStatus: (status) => status != null && status < 400)` specifically so dio "never auto-follow[s] into the signed-storage host" (the method's own doc, lines 88-90).
  - **Impacted consumer or site:** `export-download-get` calls reach this method via `ExportRemoteDataSource.getDownloadUrl` (`lib/features/export/data/datasources/export_remote_data_source.dart:79-90`), ultimately driven by `ExportJobCubit._download` (`lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart`).
  - **Existing test evidence:**
    - Unit test `test/core/network/api_client_test.dart:406-446` (group "spec-7-2 — getRedirectLocation") stubs `mockDio.get<dynamic>(any(), queryParameters: any(named: 'queryParameters'), options: any(named: 'options'))` to return a canned 302 response unconditionally. The subsequent `verify(...).captured` (lines 437-445) only captures the URL and `queryParameters` — the `options` argument (and therefore `followRedirects`/`validateStatus`) is matched with `any()`, never captured or asserted.
    - E2E test `test/features/export/export_flow_e2e_test.dart:385-419` swaps `sl<Dio>().httpClientAdapter` for a hand-written `_FakeHttpClientAdapter` (lines 22-66, wired at line 60: `sl<Dio>().httpClientAdapter = adapter`). Its `fetch()` just pops a canned response off a queue — it never reads `options.followRedirects`. I checked the real `dio` package (`dio-5.11.1`): `followRedirects` is consumed only inside `lib/src/adapters/io_adapter.dart:138` (`request.followRedirects = options.followRedirects`), never in `dio_mixin.dart`'s core pipeline. Since the fake adapter replaces exactly that layer, the e2e test's own doc comment ("proving the custom followRedirects/validateStatus combination plays correctly") only actually holds for `validateStatus` — that one genuinely runs inside the real, unfaked core (`dio_mixin.dart:633`: `final statusOk = reqOpt.validateStatus(...)`). `followRedirects` is bypassed by construction in both tests.
  - **Missing verification:** no test asserts that the `Options` instance actually sent to the transport carries `followRedirects: false`, nor exercises a real adapter-level redirect to show it's suppressed.
  - **Demonstration:** flip (or drop) `followRedirects: false` in `getRedirectLocation`. The mocked unit test still passes, since mocktail's stub returns the canned 302 regardless of the `options` it was invoked with. The e2e test still passes too, since its fake adapter also returns the queued 302+Location response unconditionally, never consulting that field. In a real build, though, dio's real `IOHttpClientAdapter` would now actually follow the 302 into the signed-storage host, so the method would observe the storage response (typically with no `Location` header) instead of the redirect itself — exactly the regression the flag exists to prevent, per the method's own doc at `api_client.dart:88-90`.

# Step 3: Triage

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings from all layers into a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

## NEXT

Read fully and follow `./step-04-present.md`

12	/// The export bottom sheet (spec-7-1) — Tela 4's own "Export job card"
13	/// overlay (`cerne-prototype.html`), its 5 states (Pendente/Processando/
14	/// Concluído/Narrativa falhou/Período vazio) swapped in place by one
15	/// `BlocBuilder` over [cubit]'s own [ExportJobState] — the sheet itself
16	/// never closes/reopens mid-job (Boundaries); every state keeps "Fechar"
17	/// at the bottom (UX-DR15).
18	///
19	/// Mirrors `EntriesFilterSheet.show()`'s own choreography
20	/// (`isScrollControlled`, `useSafeArea`, `colorScrimHeavy`, a
21	/// Reduce-Motion-aware `durationSheetUp` entrance/exit) — Code Map.
22	/// [cubit] is a fresh, `get_it`-factory-scoped instance the caller has
23	/// already started (`ExportJobCubit.start()`) before ever showing this
24	/// sheet (Boundaries: "Create fails → inline error, sheet never opens") —
25	/// closed here, once the sheet is gone, mirroring `InsertionModal.
26	/// show()`'s own cubit-disposal convention; the caller never has to
27	/// remember to do this itself.
28	class ExportStatusSheet extends StatelessWidget {
29	  const ExportStatusSheet({required this.cubit, super.key});
30	
31	  final ExportJobCubit cubit;
32	
33	  static Future<void> show(
34	    BuildContext context, {
35	    required ExportJobCubit cubit,
36	  }) async {
37	    final reduceMotion = MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations;
38	    final controller =
39	        BottomSheet.createAnimationController(Navigator.of(context))
40	          ..duration = reduceMotion
41	              ? Duration.zero
42	              : DesignTokens.durationSheetUp
43	          ..reverseDuration = reduceMotion ? Duration.zero : null;
44	    try {
45	      await showModalBottomSheet<void>(
46	        context: context,
47	        isScrollControlled: true,
48	        useSafeArea: true,
49	        barrierColor: DesignTokens.colorScrimHeavy,
50	        backgroundColor: Colors.transparent,
51	        elevation: 0,
52	        transitionAnimationController: controller,
53	        builder: (_) => ExportStatusSheet(cubit: cubit),
54	      );
55	    } finally {
56	      // Same "wait for the exit animation before disposing the
57	      // controller" rationale as `EntriesFilterSheet.show()`'s own
58	      // `finally` block.
59	      if (!controller.isDismissed) {
60	        final animationDone = Completer<void>();
61	        void onStatusChange(AnimationStatus status) {
62	          if (status == AnimationStatus.dismissed) {
63	            animationDone.complete();
64	          }
65	        }
66	
67	        controller.addStatusListener(onStatusChange);
68	        await animationDone.future;
69	        controller.removeStatusListener(onStatusChange);
70	      }
71	      controller.dispose();
72	      // The one-shot factory cubit's own disposal — mirrors
73	      // `InsertionModal.show()`'s own `await cubit.close()` convention;
74	      // cancels `ExportJobCubit`'s internal poll `Timer` too (its own
75	      // `close()` override).
76	      await cubit.close();
77	    }
78	  }
79	
80	  @override
81	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
82	    return Container(
83	      width: double.infinity,
84	      padding: DesignTokens.exportSheetPadding,
85	      decoration: const BoxDecoration(
86	        color: DesignTokens.colorSurfaceElevated,
87	        borderRadius: BorderRadius.vertical(
88	          top: Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusLg),
89	        ),
90	        boxShadow: DesignTokens.elevation2,
91	      ),
92	      child: SafeArea(
93	        top: false,
94	        child: BlocBuilder<ExportJobCubit, ExportJobState>(
95	          bloc: cubit,
96	          builder: (context, state) {
97	            return Column(
98	              mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
99	              crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
100	              children: [
101	                // Review finding (blind-hunter layer) — `liveRegion: true`
102	                // so a screen reader announces each poll-driven stage
103	                // change (Pendente → Processando → Concluído/Erro) instead
104	                // of staying silent until the user manually re-explores
105	                // the sheet.
106	                Semantics(
107	                  liveRegion: true,
108	                  child: Column(
109	                    mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
110	                    crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
111	                    children: _contentFor(context, cubit, state),
112	                  ),
113	                ),
114	                const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.spacingXs),
115	                AppButton(
116	                  label: 'Fechar',
117	                  variant: AppButtonVariant.textGhost,
118	                  textColor: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary,
119	                  onPressed: () => Navigator.of(context).pop(),
120	                ),

133	/// verbatim) — `data_ready` is the exact same "narrative still generating"
134	/// visual, just with an enabled download button appended beneath it.
135	const _generatingSequence = <Widget>[
136	  _StatusSpinner(),
137	  SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.exportStatusContentGap),
138	  _StatusText('Gerando resumo com IA...'),
139	  SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.exportStatusContentGap),

143	/// Builds this sheet's own per-state content, above the always-present
144	/// "Fechar" link — a plain top-level function (not a `switch` expression
145	/// return type juggling `Widget` vs `List<Widget>`) so each case can emit
146	/// more than one widget (icon + text + progress bar/buttons) without an
147	/// extra wrapping `Column` per case. [context]/[cubit] are only actually
148	/// used by the two cases that render a live download button
149	/// ([ExportJobDataReady]/[ExportJobDone]) — threaded through every case
150	/// regardless, so the `switch` stays one expression.
151	List<Widget> _contentFor(
152	  BuildContext context,
153	  ExportJobCubit cubit,
154	  ExportJobState state,
155	) => switch (state) {
156	  ExportJobPreparing() => const [
157	    _StatusSpinner(),
158	    SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.exportStatusContentGap),
159	    _StatusText('Preparando exportação...'),
160	  ],
161	  ExportJobGenerating() => _generatingSequence,
162	  ExportJobDataReady() => [
163	    ..._generatingSequence,
164	    const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.exportStatusContentGap),

166	      label: 'Baixar dados brutos',

168	      onPressed: () => _handleDownload(context, cubit.downloadRawData),
169	    ),
170	  ],
171	  ExportJobDone(outcome: final outcome) => _doneContent(
172	    context,
173	    cubit,
174	    outcome,
175	  ),
176	  ExportJobError() => const [
177	    Icon(
178	      Icons.error_outline,
179	      size: DesignTokens.exportStatusIconSize,
180	      color: DesignTokens.colorError,
181	    ),
182	    SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.exportStatusContentGap),
183	    _StatusText(
184	      'Não foi possível gerar a exportação.',
185	      color: DesignTokens.colorError,
186	    ),

189	    _StatusText('Nenhum registro nesse período.'),
190	    SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.spacingSm),
191	    _StatusText(
192	      'Ajuste o filtro de período e tente de novo.',
193	      color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary,
194	    ),

199	/// "Narrativa falhou/pulada" rows) — spec-7-2: both buttons now wired to a
200	/// real download via [_handleDownload], never `onPressed: null`.
201	List<Widget> _doneContent(
202	  BuildContext context,
203	  ExportJobCubit cubit,
204	  ExportOutcome outcome,
205	) {
206	  if (outcome == ExportOutcome.narrativeReady) {
207	    return [
208	      const Icon(

212	      ),

214	      const _StatusText('Resumo pronto'),
215	      const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.exportStatusContentGap),
216	      Row(
217	        children: [
218	          Expanded(
219	            child: AppButton(
220	              label: 'Baixar PDF',
221	              onPressed: () => _handleDownload(context, cubit.downloadPdf),
222	            ),
223	          ),
224	          const SizedBox(width: DesignTokens.exportStatusButtonGap),
225	          Expanded(
226	            child: AppButton(
227	              label: 'Baixar dados brutos',
228	              variant: AppButtonVariant.secondaryOutline,
229	              onPressed: () => _handleDownload(context, cubit.downloadRawData),
230	            ),
231	          ),
232	        ],
233	      ),
234	    ];
235	  }
236	  return [
237	    const Icon(
238	      Icons.error_outline,
239	      size: DesignTokens.exportStatusIconSize,
240	      color: DesignTokens.colorError,
241	    ),
242	    const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.exportStatusContentGap),
243	    const _StatusText(
244	      'Não foi possível gerar o resumo — a narrativa falhou, mas seus '
245	      'dados continuam disponíveis.',
246	      color: DesignTokens.colorError,
247	    ),
248	    const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.exportStatusContentGap),
249	    AppButton(
250	      label: 'Baixar dados brutos',
251	      variant: AppButtonVariant.secondaryOutline,
252	      onPressed: () => _handleDownload(context, cubit.downloadRawData),

255	}

257	/// Routes a download-button tap through [download] (`cubit.downloadPdf`/
258	/// `cubit.downloadRawData`, bound), then surfaces whatever `Failure` it
259	/// resolves to — if any — as an inline `SnackBar`, mirroring
260	/// `_onExportTap`'s own create-failure pattern
261	/// (`meus_registros_screen.dart`). Reads the outcome straight off
262	/// [download]'s own return value (review finding, code review patch
263	/// item 6 — a shared mutable field on the cubit, written by the cubit and

267	Future<void> _handleDownload(

2	// from the private fields they initialize, so an initializing formal
3	// (which would force the external name to match) isn't a clean fit here.

5	import 'dart:convert';

7	import 'package:dio/dio.dart';
8	import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

11	import '../failure/failure.dart';

13	import 'dio_error_code.dart';
14	import 'header_interceptor.dart';
15	import 'url_builder.dart';
16	
17	/// AD-2/AD-5 — the one network façade every repository's data source calls
18	/// through. Builds the real URL via `UrlBuilder`, sends the request through
19	/// `dio` (header + retry interceptors already attached in DI), and maps
20	/// every outcome — success or failure — to `Either<Failure, T>`; no
21	/// dio/native exception ever escapes unmapped (RNF09).
22	///
23	/// Story 1.5: also the one detection point for a mid-session `AUTH_EXPIRED`
24	/// — signals [SessionExpiryNotifier] when one is seen outside
25	/// `HeaderInterceptor.anonKeyOnlyFunctions`, so the boot-time `auth-refresh`
26	/// call (Story 1.4's `restoreSession()`) never triggers it.
27	///
28	/// Tests mock this interface directly (per the architecture spine's testing
29	/// convention), not a fake transport layer underneath it.
30	class ApiClient {
31	  ApiClient({
32	    required Dio dio,
33	    required UrlBuilder urlBuilder,
34	    required SessionExpiryNotifier sessionExpiryNotifier,
35	  }) : _dio = dio,
36	       _urlBuilder = urlBuilder,
37	       _sessionExpiryNotifier = sessionExpiryNotifier;
38	
39	  final Dio _dio;
40	  final UrlBuilder _urlBuilder;
41	  final SessionExpiryNotifier _sessionExpiryNotifier;
42	
43	  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> get(
44	    String function, {
45	    List<String> pathParams = const [],
46	    Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,
47	  }) => _send(
48	    () => _dio.get<Map<String, dynamic>>(
49	      _urlBuilder.build(function, pathParams),
50	      queryParameters: queryParameters,
51	    ),
52	  );
53	
54	  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> post(
55	    String function, {
56	    List<String> pathParams = const [],
57	    Object? data,
58	  }) => _send(
59	    () => _dio.post<Map<String, dynamic>>(
60	      _urlBuilder.build(function, pathParams),
61	      data: data,
62	    ),
63	  );
64	
65	  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> patch(
66	    String function, {
67	    List<String> pathParams = const [],
68	    Object? data,
69	  }) => _send(
70	    () => _dio.patch<Map<String, dynamic>>(
71	      _urlBuilder.build(function, pathParams),
72	      data: data,
73	    ),
74	  );
75	
76	  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> delete(
77	    String function, {
78	    List<String> pathParams = const [],
79	    Object? data,
80	  }) => _send(
81	    () => _dio.delete<Map<String, dynamic>>(
82	      _urlBuilder.build(function, pathParams),
83	      data: data,
84	    ),
85	  );
86	
87	  /// spec-7-2 — `export-download-get`'s own shape: the real payload is the
88	  /// `302` response's `Location` header (a signed Storage URL), never a
89	  /// JSON body. `followRedirects: false` stops dio from auto-following
90	  /// into that signed-storage host itself (Boundaries); the permissive
91	  /// `validateStatus` (anything below 400) keeps dio from throwing on the
92	  /// `302` the way its own default validator (`>= 200 && < 300`) would.
93	  /// `responseType` is deliberately left at its default — an *error*
94	  /// response (>= 400) still decodes as JSON, so `_mapDioException`/
95	  /// `dioErrorCodeOf` keep mapping it exactly as they do for every other
96	  /// call on this façade, unchanged.
97	  ///
98	  /// A `302` with no `Location` header (shouldn't happen — the contract's
99	  /// own response is declared as exactly this) maps to
100	  /// [Failure.malformedResponse] rather than returning an empty/null URL
101	  /// (RNF09, I/O matrix: "Missing Location").
102	  Future<Either<Failure, String>> getRedirectLocation(
103	    String function, {
104	    List<String> pathParams = const [],
105	    Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,
106	  }) async {
107	    try {
108	      final response = await _dio.get<dynamic>(
109	        _urlBuilder.build(function, pathParams),
110	        queryParameters: queryParameters,
111	        options: Options(
112	          followRedirects: false,
113	          validateStatus: (status) => status != null && status < 400,
114	        ),
115	      );
116	      final location = response.headers.value('location');
117	      if (location == null) {
118	        return left(
119	          const Failure.malformedResponse(message: 'Missing Location header'),
120	        );
121	      }
122	      return right(location);
123	    } on DioException catch (e) {

2	  summary: No portrait-only orientation lock is enforced anywhere in the app shell (`ios/Runner/Info.plist` still lists landscape orientations alongside portrait).
3	  evidence: `docs/input/requirements.md` fixes the app to a single 390x844 portrait-only frame with no landscape path, but Story 1.1 is core infrastructure only (no screens/app-shell UI) and the architecture spine doesn't assign this lock to any specific story. Likely belongs to Story 1.6 (Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders), the first story that builds real app-shell UI — should be picked up there rather than silently falling through the cracks.

6	  summary: `lib/core/widgets/avatar.dart`'s `Avatar` renders raw initials text with no `Semantics` wrapper, so a screen reader announces e.g. "W D" instead of something like "Avatar, Wagner Duarte".
7	  evidence: Accessibility semantics were never required by Story 1.2's spec (no boundary, acceptance criterion, or epic-context requirement mentions it) and the prototype gives no guidance either, so adding it now would be scope creep beyond the frozen intent. Worth a deliberate pass across all shared widgets (button/text-field/avatar) once an accessibility requirement exists, rather than bolting it onto one widget ad hoc.

Not required by Story 1.2's boundaries (§6's button component table lists only normal/pressed/disabled variations) — pick up when the first async-submit screen (Story 1.3) needs it, rather than letting each feature improvise its own busy treatment.

No domain code exists yet to violate this, so it's not a bug today — worth a lint rule or architecture test once the first feature's `domain/` layer is scaffolded.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:** one task per Code Map bullet above, in that order, plus:
- [x] Unit tests: `getRedirectLocation` (success/missing-location/error-status), `getDownloadUrl`, `toState()`'s `data_ready`, cubit download methods
- [x] Widget tests: hybrid-state render, both `done` buttons call through, download failure → `SnackBar` with state unchanged

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given `status=data_ready`/`narrativeStatus=processing`, when polled, then "Baixar dados brutos" is already enabled and downloads via `GET /export/:jobId/download` while summary-progress text stays visible underneath.
- Given the narrative fails/is skipped at `status=done`, then "Baixar dados brutos" stays enabled, error copy stays scoped to the narrative.
- Given the narrative succeeds at `status=done`, then both "Baixar PDF" and "Baixar dados brutos" are enabled and tappable.

### Review Findings

_Code review (lib/ group, 2026-11-07) — chunked review; test/ and docs/metadata groups pending in follow-up rounds._

  Reviewed the spec and the full test-only diff (both halves) against the three ACs and the Tasks checklist.
  
  ## Findings
  
  - **Title: In-flight-guard test exercises cross-format calls but asserts same-format blocking behavior, contradicting the already-fixed per-format guard**
    **Violates:** Tasks checklist item "cubit download methods" (unit tests)
    **Evidence:** In `test/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit_test.dart`, the diff adds (diff lines ~2548–2585):
    ```dart
    test('review finding (patch item 3): a second download call arriving '
        'while the first is still in flight is a no-op — _downloadInFlight '
        'stops it from ever reaching the repository/opener, mirroring '
        '_pollInFlight\'s own overlap guard', () {
      ...
      unawaited(cubit.downloadPdf().then((value) => firstResult = value));
      async.flushMicrotasks();
      unawaited(
        cubit.downloadRawData().then((value) {   // <-- different format
          secondResult = value;
          secondCompleted = true;
        }),
      );
      async.flushMicrotasks();
  
      expect(repository.getDownloadUrlCalls, hasLength(1));   // <-- expects it was blocked
      expect(secondCompleted, isTrue);
      expect(secondResult, isNull);
    ```
    But the reviewed/patched implementation (`lib/features/export/presentation/cubit/export_job_cubit.dart:149`, Review Findings item 1 in the spec) deliberately keys the in-flight guard by format — `final Set<ExportDownloadFormat> _downloadsInFlight = {};` — specifically *so that* a concurrent tap on the *other* format's button is never blocked ("a single shared flag silently dropped a legitimate, concurrent tap on the other format's button… so the two formats never block each other"). Tracing the actual code: `downloadPdf()` adds `pdf` to the set and suspends on the repository call; `downloadRawData()` then checks `_downloadsInFlight.contains(raw)` → false → proceeds, reaches the repository, and resolves immediately. So `repository.getDownloadUrlCalls` would actually be length 2, not 1, and the test as written would fail against the very implementation it's meant to verify. The test exercises the wrong scenario (cross-format instead of same-format) and asserts behavior that is the opposite of the documented fix.
  
    **Note for context:** the live working tree (uncommitted, beyond this diff) already has this corrected — the test now calls `downloadPdf()` twice (same format) for the blocking assertion, and a new sibling test ("review finding (round 2): a download for the OTHER format … is NOT blocked") correctly asserts `getDownloadUrlCalls` reaches length 2 for cross-format concurrency. So this exact defect has since been fixed, just not reflected in the diff file that was handed to me for review.
  
  ## Checklist / AC coverage (otherwise)

64	+---

66	+<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
67	+
68	+## Intent
69	+
70	+**Problem:** Spec-7-1 left both download buttons `onPressed: null` and folded `data_ready` into the same visual as `processing` — raw data is never actually downloadable, even once the backend has it ready ahead of the narrative.
71	+
72	+**Approach:** Wire `GET /export/:jobId/download` behind both buttons (open the signed URL externally, never buffer it in-app), and give `data_ready` its own state so the sheet shows "Baixar dados brutos" already enabled while the narrative keeps processing underneath.
73	+
74	+## Boundaries & Constraints
75	+
76	+**Always:**
77	+- Call `export-download-get` by function name, `jobId` trailing, `format=pdf|raw` query param.
78	+- Capture the `302`'s `Location` header directly (`followRedirects: false` + a permissive `validateStatus`) — never auto-follow into the signed-storage host.
79	+- Open the signed URL externally (new `DownloadOpener` port, `url_launcher`-backed) — never buffer/write the file in-app.
80	+- `data_ready` → its own `ExportJobState.dataReady()`: same progress-bar/text as `generating`, plus the now-enabled raw button beneath.
81	+- A download failure shows an inline `SnackBar` (mirrors `_onExportTap`'s create-failure pattern), never mutates the sheet's job-status content.
82	+
83	+**Ask First:** None — docs/input is silent on how a finished file reaches the user; external-open vs. in-app buffering is decided here.
84	+
85	+**Never:** add a new `Failure` subtype for download errors (reuse `Failure.fromCode`, AD-3); touch empty-period state/copy (Story 7.3); add a busy state to `AppButton` itself (deferred).
86	+
87	+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
88	+
89	+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output | Error Handling |
90	+|----------|--------------|------------------|-----------------|
91	+| Hybrid state | `status=data_ready`, `narrativeStatus=processing` | Progress bar + text + enabled "Baixar dados brutos" | N/A |
92	+| Raw/PDF tap | Tap enabled button | `GET export-download-get?format=raw\|pdf` → opens URL externally | Failure → `SnackBar`, state unchanged |
93	+| Narrative failed/skipped | `status=done`, `narrativeStatus in {failed,skipped}` | Only raw button, now enabled | N/A |
94	+| Missing `Location` | `302` with no header | `Failure.malformedResponse` | Same `SnackBar` path |
95	+
96	+</frozen-after-approval>
97	+
98	+## Code Map
99	+

+---
+title: 'Narrative-Independent Raw-Data Download'
+type: 'feature'
+created: '2026-11-07'
+status: 'done'
+review_loop_iteration: 0
+context: []

+
+<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
+
+## Intent
+
+**Problem:** Spec-7-1 left both download buttons `onPressed: null` and folded `data_ready` into the same visual as `processing` — raw data is never actually downloadable, even once the backend has it ready ahead of the narrative.
+
+**Approach:** Wire `GET /export/:jobId/download` behind both buttons (open the signed URL externally, never buffer it in-app), and give `data_ready` its own state so the sheet shows "Baixar dados brutos" already enabled while the narrative keeps processing underneath.
+
+## Boundaries & Constraints
+
+**Always:**
+- Call `export-download-get` by function name, `jobId` trailing, `format=pdf|raw` query param.
+- Capture the `302`'s `Location` header directly (`followRedirects: false` + a permissive `validateStatus`) — never auto-follow into the signed-storage host.
+- Open the signed URL externally (new `DownloadOpener` port, `url_launcher`-backed) — never buffer/write the file in-app.
+- `data_ready` → its own `ExportJobState.dataReady()`: same progress-bar/text as `generating`, plus the now-enabled raw button beneath.
+- A download failure shows an inline `SnackBar` (mirrors `_onExportTap`'s create-failure pattern), never mutates the sheet's job-status content.
+
+**Ask First:** None — docs/input is silent on how a finished file reaches the user; external-open vs. in-app buffering is decided here.
+
+**Never:** add a new `Failure` subtype for download errors (reuse `Failure.fromCode`, AD-3); touch empty-period state/copy (Story 7.3); add a busy state to `AppButton` itself (deferred).
+
+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
+
+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output | Error Handling |
+|----------|--------------|------------------|-----------------|
+| Hybrid state | `status=data_ready`, `narrativeStatus=processing` | Progress bar + text + enabled "Baixar dados brutos" | N/A |

# Test Automation Summary

## Scope

Flutter/Dart project — "E2E" here means the project's own established
convention of `*_flow_e2e_test.dart` files: the real DI graph (`sl`),
real `Cubit` -> `Repository` -> `DataSource` -> `ApiClient` -> `Dio`
pipeline (both real interceptors attached), with only the transport
boundary (`HttpClientAdapter`) and native plugins faked (no
device/simulator/CI exists yet per AGENTS.md). Playwright/browser E2E
does not apply to this codebase.

Target feature: **export** (story 7.1 — request a period export & job
status tracking), chosen because capture, entries, and chat already had
this level of coverage; export did not.

## Generated Tests

### E2E Tests

- [x] `test/features/export/export_flow_e2e_test.dart` — 5 tests, driven
  directly against the real, DI-resolved `ExportJobCubit`:
  - Happy path: `start()` → genuine `export-summary-create` POST (URL,
    headers, periodEnd bumped to local end-of-day before UTC
    conversion) → real `Timer.periodic` poll loop → genuine
    `export-status-get/{jobId}` GETs → Pendente → Processando →
    Concluído (`ExportOutcome.narrativeReady`); also asserts polling
    really stops once terminal.
  - Narrativa falhou: `narrativeStatus: failed` maps to
    `ExportOutcome.narrativeUnavailable` through the real DTO mapping.
  - Período vazio: `errorCode: EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` maps through the
    real `Failure.fromCode` → `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()`.
  - Erro: a non-empty-period error code (`AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`) maps
    to the generic `ExportJobState.error`.
  - Review-patch coverage: `export-summary-create` failing with a
    *retryable* code (`RATE_LIMITED`) is never retried — proves
    `RetryInterceptor.neverRetriedFunctions`' real wiring for this
    function (previously only exercised in isolation or against a fake
    repository, never through the real Dio pipeline).

This complements, and does not duplicate, existing coverage:
`export_job_cubit_test.dart` (fake repository, I/O-matrix transitions),
`export_remote_data_source_test.dart` (mocked `ApiClient`, DTO
decoding), `export_status_sheet_test.dart` (widget rendering per
state), and `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`'s "export entry point"
group (tap → picker → `start()` → sheet, against a fake repository).
None of those drove a real network/poll round trip end to end.

### API Tests

Not applicable separately — the backend contract is exercised through
the same e2e suite above (real `ApiClient`/`Dio`/interceptors against a
faked transport), consistent with how every other feature in this
project is tested (no standalone HTTP-level test layer exists outside
this pattern).

## Verification

- `fvm flutter analyze` — 0 issues
- `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` — clean (after one auto-format
  pass)
- `fvm flutter test` — **1100/1100 passed**, no regressions in the
  existing suite

## Coverage

- Features with `*_flow_e2e_test.dart` coverage: capture, entries,
  chat, **export** (new)
- Still missing this level of coverage: auth, account, vault (epic 8 —
  dashboard/profile/logout/account-deletion — is still `backlog`, so
  N/A for now)

## Next Steps

- Consider the same real-pipeline e2e treatment for auth (login/refresh/
  expired-session recovery) and vault (biometric/PIN gate) when their
  own review cycles come up.
- Story 7.2 (independent raw-data download) will need its own e2e
  additions once the download taps are wired for real — this suite's
  "done" tests intentionally only assert the disabled-button state that
  exists today.

Flutter/Dart project — "E2E" here means the project's own established
convention of `*_flow_e2e_test.dart` files: the real DI graph (`sl`),
real `Cubit` -> `Repository` -> `DataSource` -> `ApiClient` -> `Dio`
pipeline (both real interceptors attached), with only the transport
boundary (`HttpClientAdapter`) and native plugins faked (no
device/simulator/CI exists yet per AGENTS.md). Playwright/browser E2E
does not apply to this codebase.

Target feature: **export** (story 7.1 — request a period export & job
status tracking), chosen because capture, entries, and chat already had
this level of coverage; export did not.

## Generated Tests

### E2E Tests

- [x] `test/features/export/export_flow_e2e_test.dart` — 5 tests, driven
  directly against the real, DI-resolved `ExportJobCubit`:
  - Happy path: `start()` → genuine `export-summary-create` POST (URL,
    headers, periodEnd bumped to local end-of-day before UTC
    conversion) → real `Timer.periodic` poll loop → genuine
    `export-status-get/{jobId}` GETs → Pendente → Processando →
    Concluído (`ExportOutcome.narrativeReady`); also asserts polling
    really stops once terminal.
  - Narrativa falhou: `narrativeStatus: failed` maps to
    `ExportOutcome.narrativeUnavailable` through the real DTO mapping.
  - Período vazio: `errorCode: EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` maps through the
    real `Failure.fromCode` → `ExportJobState.emptyPeriod()`.
  - Erro: a non-empty-period error code (`AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`) maps
    to the generic `ExportJobState.error`.
  - Review-patch coverage: `export-summary-create` failing with a
    *retryable* code (`RATE_LIMITED`) is never retried — proves
    `RetryInterceptor.neverRetriedFunctions`' real wiring for this
    function (previously only exercised in isolation or against a fake
    repository, never through the real Dio pipeline).

This complements, and does not duplicate, existing coverage:
`export_job_cubit_test.dart` (fake repository, I/O-matrix transitions),
`export_remote_data_source_test.dart` (mocked `ApiClient`, DTO
decoding), `export_status_sheet_test.dart` (widget rendering per
state), and `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`'s "export entry point"
group (tap → picker → `start()` → sheet, against a fake repository).
None of those drove a real network/poll round trip end to end.

### API Tests

Not applicable separately — the backend contract is exercised through
the same e2e suite above (real `ApiClient`/`Dio`/interceptors against a
faked transport), consistent with how every other feature in this
project is tested (no standalone HTTP-level test layer exists outside
this pattern).

## Verification

- `fvm flutter analyze` — 0 issues
- `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` — clean (after one auto-format
  pass)
- `fvm flutter test` — **1100/1100 passed**, no regressions in the
  existing suite

## Coverage

- Features with `*_flow_e2e_test.dart` coverage: capture, entries,
  chat, **export** (new)
- Still missing this level of coverage: auth, account, vault (epic 8 —
  dashboard/profile/logout/account-deletion — is still `backlog`, so
  N/A for now)

## Next Steps

- Consider the same real-pipeline e2e treatment for auth (login/refresh/
  expired-session recovery) and vault (biometric/PIN gate) when their
  own review cycles come up.
- Story 7.2 (independent raw-data download) will need its own e2e
  additions once the download taps are wired for real — this suite's
  "done" tests intentionally only assert the disabled-button state that
  exists today.
